    RELATED CODE SECTIONS & RESOURCES
    Chapter 5, Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York (Dining Out NYC Rules),
    New York City Administrative Code (Administrative Code) Section 19-160(a),
    Title 1 RCNY §101-14


 I. BACKGROUND
    Existing enclosed sidewalk cafes must comply with the applicable Department of Transportation (DOT) Dining
    Out NYC Rules, which went into effect on March 3, 2024. New enclosed sidewalk cafes are no longer
    permitted and the New York City Zoning Resolution provisions and Department of Consumer and Worker
    Protection rules relating to enclosed sidewalk cafes have been repealed. As described herein, only certain
    eligible previously approved enclosed sidewalk cafes are permitted to continue operating.
    The Department of Buildings (DOB) issues the following guidance regarding alterations and permitted work
    for existing enclosed sidewalk cafes as described below in Section II of this Bulletin.


 II. EXISTING ENCLOSED SIDEWALK CAFES (located beyond the property lines)
    An existing enclosed sidewalk cafe located beyond the property lines may continue to operate provided such
    enclosed sidewalk cafe was constructed pursuant to a permit issued by DOB prior to March 16, 2020.
    Pursuant to section 28-102.4 of the NYC Administrative Code and section 102.6 of the NYC Building Code,
    the lawful use of the existing enclosed sidewalk cafe is allowed to continue without change except as
    otherwise deemed necessary by DOB. Only ordinary repairs, maintenance, and minor alterations, as
    described below, will be allowed. Enclosed sidewalk cafe structures must be maintained in accordance with
    NYC Administrative Code Section 28-301.1.
    DOB no longer reviews or issues permits for existing enclosed sidewalk cafes that are located beyond the
    property lines.


 III. PERMITTED WORK
    Work done for Minor alterations and ordinary repairs as defined in Section 28-105.4.2 of the NYC
    Administrative Code, does not require a permit and is allowed for existing enclosed sidewalk cafes. In general,
    replacements or renewals of existing work in the existing enclosed sidewalk cafe with the same or equivalent
    materials or equipment parts, that do not in any way affect health or the fire or structural safety of the building,

   IV. WORK NOT PERMITTED
      Work that is defined in section 28-105.4.2 of the Administrative Code as work not constituting minor
      alterations and ordinary repairs is not permitted. In general, that includes work that affects health or the fire
      or structural safety of the building or the safe use of the space. Therefore, changes or alterations to a
      previously permitted existing enclosed sidewalk cafe structure, including but not limited to, any change to
      the number of occupants in the certificate of occupancy (CO), cafe footprint, size, height, ceiling, exterior
      wall transparency, elevation, and the introduction of permanent fixtures, are not allowed.


   V. TEMPORARY OUTDOOR DINING STRUCTURES CONSTRUCTED DURING
      COVID PURSUANT TO EMERGENCY EXECUTIVE ORDER 126 (March 17,
      (March 17, 2020 – March 2, 2024)
      The temporary Open Restaurants program was established pursuant to an emergency executive order in
      response to the COVID-19 pandemic and permitted temporary outdoor dining structures to be constructed.
      Such temporary outdoor dining structures were permitted to be constructed without construction permits
      from DOB, or Department of Consumer and Worker Protection licenses, and were not subject to zoning
      requirements. As of March 3, 2024, these structures are subject to DOT rule including subdivision (b) of
      Section §5-13 that states in relevant parts:
        “A restaurant operating a temporary outdoor dining setup that does not submit a petition for a revocable
        consent pursuant this chapter within five (5) months of the effective date of these rules shall immediately
        remove such temporary outdoor dining setup. Any temporary outdoor dining setup that is not removed shall
        be subject to penalties for the operation of a sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe without a license and revocable
        consent and may be removed in accordance with paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of Section 5-12 of these
        rules.”
      Therefore, unless an application to DOT has been submitted, such a structure may be subject to removal.
      Refer to DOT Rule Section §5-13 Temporary Outdoor Dining Structures for more information.


   VI. SIDEWALK CAFES & ROADWAY CAFES OTHER THAN EXISTING
       ENCLOSED SIDEWALK CAFES
      Refer to Buildings Bulletin BB 2024-005 for more information on sidewalk cafes and roadway cafes that are
      beyond the property lines and outdoor cafes located within the property lines.
